topic.title: Ceded Karelia and border irredentism ('ceded' vs 'occupied')

queries.text: debate on returning ceded Karelia to Finland and calling the ceded areas occupied
luovutetun Karjalan palautuskeskustelu, luovutetut vai miehitetyt alueet
Finnish irredentism and the lost eastern territories
debatten om att återlämna det avträdda Karelen till Finland

items.label: contested
items.description: Replaces 'ceded' (luovutettu) with 'occupied' (miehitetty) throughout the Karelia question article, renames the debate 'Karjala takaisin' ('Karelia back') and adds that Finland took no position on the border in 1990 'for some completely incomprehensible reason'.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted from the added text: 'Miehitetty Karjala' ('Occupied Karelia'), 'miehitettyjen alueiden palautuskeskustelu' ('debate on returning the occupied areas'), 'Karjala takaisin-kysymykseksi' ('the Karelia-back question') and 'jostain täysin käsittämättömästä syystä' ('for some completely incomprehensible reason'): it reframes the ceded areas as occupied throughout the lead and history, and adds an external link (kavkaz.fi). Community dispute: the removal summary objects to the term, 'termin "miehitetyt alueet" voi esitellä artikkelissa, mutta ei joka tilanteessa' ('the term "occupied areas" can be presented in the article, but not in every context'), i.e. neutrality of wording. Ten edits by one anonymous editor (E1, 81.197.x.x) on 2005-09-26 22:42-22:57 UTC, removed by a different account (E12) about 10 h later. Candidate c01 (contains must-include 445526). Not level 3: one editor, one article, never put back, no citation changed.

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds, after a quoted Russian statement calling organisers of Karelia-return opinion polls 'provocateurs', that opponents of the occupation of the Baltic states were also once branded provocateurs, footnoted to a 1985 newspaper article hosted on kavkaz.fi.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted: 'Toisaalta myös Baltian maiden miehityksen vastustajat pyrittiin aikanaan leimaamaan provokaattoreiksi' ('On the other hand, opponents of the occupation of the Baltic states were also once branded provocateurs'), an analogy that frames the return debate, with a footnote to a 1985 Suomenmaa article via kavkaz.fi. Community dispute: put back once after a removal, and the second removal is about sourcing: '"lähde" ja väite eivät täsmää' ('the "source" and the claim do not match'). Added by E20 on 2006-04-15 (1017438), rolled back by E21 after 5.8 h with no reason (1018667), put back the next morning by E22 (1019509; summary 'Poistot kannattaa perustella, ettei tule palautuksia', 'removals should be justified, so that they do not get restored') and removed 8 min later by E8 (1019516). Candidates c15, c28 (identical text). Not level 3: E20 and E22 are both 83.102.x.x (one editor), one article, one re-insertion within a day; the source mismatch could count as the sources signal, but level 3 also needs an editors or articles signal.

items.label: reverted
items.description: Adds Greater Finland to the list of proposed solutions to the Karelia question: East Karelia could also be joined to Finland.
items.why: Level 1. Substantive text by an anonymous editor (E17, 80.221.x.x) taken out by a different account (E10) after 4 min with a plain rollback summary. Content: 'Suomen yhteyteen voitaisiin liittää myös Itä-Karjala, jolloin muodostuisi Suur-Suomi' ('East Karelia could also be joined to Finland, which would form Greater Finland') adds an irredentist option, but there is no dispute signal: no reason given, never put back, no edit war, no template. Candidate c33.

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds that Finland handed the ceded areas' property register to the Soviet Union and that, as the Soviet Union did not nationalise that property, it still belongs to the original owners and their heirs (with a quote of the 1947 Paris peace treaty).
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted: 'Kun Neuvostoliitto ei kansallistanut tätä omaisuutta, se kuuluu edelleen alkuperäisille omistajille ja heidän perijöilleen' ('As the Soviet Union did not nationalise this property, it still belongs to the original owners and their heirs'), a legal claim about property in ceded Karelia. Community dispute: a citation-needed template was attached to it the same day ('{{lähde|kaksi ed. lausetta, 30.8.2010}}', 'source needed: the two previous sentences') and the removal summary is about sourcing: 'Erittäin radikaali väite ilman lähdettä. Ei pidä huolia artikkeliin jollei kelvollista lähdettä löydy' ('A very radical claim without a source. Should not be accepted in the article unless a valid source is found'). Added by E308 (91.156.x.x) on 2010-08-30, removed by E309 (83.148.x.x) on 2011-07-30, about 334 days later. The same removal also took out an older paragraph (a lawsuit and a law professor's view) that this edit did not add. Candidate c42 (partial-removal; the edit's sentences appear in the removed text verbatim or lightly reworded). Not level 3: one editor, one article, never put back.

items.label: reverted
items.description: Pastes the lead of the Winter War article into the history section and inserts 'pienen' ('a small') into 'in 1944 the Soviet Union reconquered part of the area'.
items.why: Level 1. Substantive text by E51 taken out by a different account (E53) after 3 min with a plain undo summary. Most of it is a copy of another article's lead (misplaced duplicate; it says Finland 'pakkoluovutti' ('was forced to cede') 13 % of its land). The one change to this article's own text, 'valloittikin pienen osan alueesta uudestaan' ('reconquered a small part of the area'), shrinks the 1944 Soviet reconquest, but there is no dispute signal: no reason given, never put back, no template. Candidate c02 (must-include 7493076).

items.label: reverted
items.description: Rewords the municipality lists from parts 'left to Finland' (Suomelle jääneet) to parts that 'stayed in Finland' (Suomessa pysyneet / Suomen alueena säilyneet), reflows the lists, adds a map of ceded Karelia and, in the last version, rewrites which areas the evacuees came from.
items.why: Level 1, capped. Taken out twice by a different account (E60), no exclusion applies. It is one side of a back-and-forth on 2013-02-15 to 03-21 (E56/E58 in 212.226.x.x and E62/E63 in 85.76.x.x against E57/E60; the page was partly protected for a month, 12702015 to 12896678). Not a claim in the §1 sense: the disputed change is phrasing that changes no fact, number, date or name ('Suomelle jääneet osat' vs 'Suomessa pysyneet osat'; the inserter's summary: 'kun jonkun kunnan osaa ei luovutettu, osa ei "jäänyt" Suomeen, vaan jatkoi olemassaoloaan eli pysyi Suomessa', 'when part of a municipality was not ceded, it did not "remain" in Finland but went on existing, i.e. stayed in Finland'), plus list layout and a map. No removal says this side is wrong: 'rv E57n muokkaukseen asti' ('rv back to E57's edit') and a rollback; the earlier revert by E57 said only 'aiempi versio oli sanonnaltaan onnistuneempi' ('the earlier version was better worded'). An edit war over wording is not a disputed claim, so it stays at level 1. The last version (12930962, E63) also rewrote the evacuee areas (summary calls the old text 'satuilu', 'fabrication'); that passage was rolled back after 2 min without a reason and never put back. Re-insertions 12701319 and 12925503 appear in the pack only as removals of the other side (c16, c29), so they cannot be listed as inserting revisions. Candidates c39, c30 (this side) and c16, c29 (the other side). E59's +3 edit (12702005) is dropped.

items.label: contested
items.description: Restructures the Karelia lead around two coats of arms and defines 'Russian Karelia, i.e. East Karelia' as the Republic of Karelia's districts mapped onto Aunus, Ladoga, Puutoinen and Viena Karelia, so that the ceded Ladoga Karelia is counted as East Karelia.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted from the added text: 'Venäjän Karjala eli Itä-Karjala käsittää Karjalan tasavallan 11 eteläistä piiriä (Aunuksen Karjala), 2 lounaisinta piiriä (Laatokan Karjala), itäisimmän piirin (Puutoisten Karjala) ja 5 pohjoista piiriä (Vienan Karjala)' ('Russian Karelia, i.e. East Karelia, comprises the Republic of Karelia's 11 southern districts (Aunus Karelia), the 2 south-westernmost (Ladoga Karelia), the easternmost (Puutoinen Karelia) and 5 northern ones (Viena Karelia)'); the inserter's summaries state 'Itä-Karjala = Karjalan Tasavalta = Venäjän Karjala' and 'Laatokan Karjala on toki Itä-Karjalaa' ('Ladoga Karelia is of course East Karelia'). The 2008-05-14/15 version also drops two {{lähde}} (citation needed) tags. Community dispute: an edit war from 2008-05-08 to 05-20 (5-7 identity reverts on the page within 3 days) with removal summaries on neutrality, accuracy and sourcing: 'määrätietoista POV-pushausta' ('determined POV-pushing', E150), 'Jo lause "Karjalan alueella on kaksi Karjalaa" on täysin järjetön' ('already the sentence "in the Karelia area there are two Karelias" is completely absurd', E8), 'vandalistista POV-pushausta' ('vandalistic POV-pushing', E151), 'nykyiset Karjalan tasavallan piirit eivät mene noin yksi yhteen historiallisten alueiden kanssa ... ei ole Puutoisen Karjalaa' ('the Republic's current districts do not map one-to-one onto the historical regions ... there is no Puutoinen Karelia', E140), 'tällaiselle väitteelle tarvitaan lähteet' ('such a claim needs sources', E149). Put back at least 7 times by one named account (E137); the first insertion 4750215 and the re-insertions 4752344, 4757069, 4757086 appear in the pack only as the other side's restored/removing revisions (c11, c04, c17), so they cannot be listed here. Not level 3: one account adds the claim on one article; persistence (put back 2+ times over 12 days) is one signal; dropped citation-needed tags are not a citation removed or replaced. Left out: 4787255 by E148 ('palautus parempaan versioon + vaakunat', 'restored to the better version + coats of arms'), which rewrote the passage without the 'eli Itä-Karjala' district mapping, so E148 is not counted as a second editor of this claim. Candidates c18, c05, c19 (this side) and c11, c04, c17 (the same war seen from the other side). See i08 for a similar district mapping added by another account five months later.

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds a map of 'Finnish and Russian Karelia' whose legend maps the Republic of Karelia's districts onto Aunus (10), Ladoga (2), Puutoinen (1) and Viena (5) Karelia, drops a citation-needed tag, and in later versions changes 'luovutti' (ceded) to 'pakkoluovutti' (was forced to cede).
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted from the added legend: 'Venäjän Karjala eli Karjalan tasavalta: Aunuksen Karjala, nykyään 10 piiriä; Laatokan Karjala, nyk. 2 piiriä; ... Vienan Karjala, nyk. 5 piiriä' ('Russian Karelia, i.e. the Republic of Karelia: Aunus Karelia, today 10 districts; Ladoga Karelia, today 2 districts; ... Viena Karelia, today 5 districts'); versions 2-4 also change 'luovutti' to 'pakkoluovutti' ('ceded' to 'was forced to cede'), and every version drops '{{Lähde||15. syyskuuta 2008}}' from the sentence on what Karelia means in Russia. Community dispute: removal summaries on accuracy, 'virheellinen kartta pois, katso tarkemmin keskustelusivu' ('erroneous map removed, see the talk page', E140) and 'Käsitteellä "Aunuksen Karjala" ei ole mitään tekemistä Karjalan tasavallan kanssa' ('the concept "Aunus Karelia" has nothing to do with the Republic of Karelia', E148); put back 3 times. One named account (E156), 2008-10-14 to 10-18, removed 4 times by three accounts (E140, E148 twice, E8); each version stayed 3 min to 19 h. Candidates c12, c08, c25, c26 (same map each time). Not level 3 within this item: one account, one article, all insertions within 4 days, the dropped tag is not a citation. For review: the district mapping is close to the one E137 added in May 2008 (i07). If both are treated as one claim, accounts (E137, E156) plus persistence (May to October) would meet level 3; kept at level 2 because the texts differ (prose vs map legend), the pack does not link them, and in doubt the lower level applies.

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds to the first sentence, before its Kotus reference, that Karelia lies between the Gulf of Finland, Saimaa, Ladoga, Onega and the White Sea.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted: 'maantieteellinen alue Suomenlahden, Saimaan, Laatokan, Äänisen ja Vienanmeren välillä, valtaosin Fennoskandian itäosassa' ('a geographic area between the Gulf of Finland, Saimaa, Ladoga, Onega and the White Sea, mostly in eastern Fennoscandia'): it sets the extent of Karelia inside the sentence footnoted to the Kotus publication 'Mistä puhutaan, kun puhutaan Karjalasta?', and a removal says the source does not support it: 'ei sisälly lähteeseen, vääristää ajatusta' ('not in the source, distorts the idea'). Community dispute: the same text was added 6 times on 2012-06-12 to 06-15 and removed 6 times by four accounts (E121 three times, E8, E39, E57); the last removal was undone once more (11772377, outside the pack). Inserting editors: E182, E183, E184 (all 193.64.x.x, one editor) and E185 (212.226.x.x), i.e. two editors; their summaries include 'Lisätty Karjalan alueen "reunavesistöt"' ('added the "border waters" of the Karelia area') and 'Miksi Karjalan suuria "reunavesistöjä" ei saisi luetella?' ('why may Karelia's large "border waters" not be listed?'). Candidates c20, c21, c22, c23, c24, c06 (identical text). Not level 3: two editors is one signal; one article, all insertions within about 3 days (persistence needs 7), and no citation was added, removed or replaced (the text went in front of an existing reference).

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds a 'motive of Greater Finland' passage: supporters wanted to save kindred peoples from ethnic cleansing or assimilation by the ruling state, Stalin wanted them liquidated, and because Greater Finland was not realised only the elderly still speak Karelian, Finnish and Vepsian in the Republic of Karelia.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted from the first version: 'Suur-Suomen kannattajilla oli usein motiivina sukulaiskielisten alueiden pelastaminen hallitsevan valtion harjoittamalta etnisiltä puhdistuksilta' ('Greater Finland's supporters often had as their motive saving kindred-language areas from ethnic cleansing by the ruling state') and 'Suur-Suomen toteuttamatta jättäminen altisti nämä kansat tilaan, josta syystä nykyään karjalan, suomen ja vepsän kielen osaaminen Karjalan tasavallassa on vain vanhusten taitona' ('not realising Greater Finland exposed these peoples to a situation because of which today only the elderly know Karelian, Finnish and Vepsian in the Republic of Karelia'): a one-sided framing of the irredentist programme. Community dispute: removed with 'puppua poistettu, tämä ei ole pamflettisivusto' ('nonsense removed, this is not a pamphlet site'); put back 23 days later in a reworded version together with the {{kiistanalainen}} (disputed) template (392859; summary 'alkuperäinen sivu palautettava keskustelun ajaksi', 'the original page must be restored for the duration of the discussion') and removed 91 s later. Both insertions by E74 (130.233.x.x). The 392859 summary says it restores a version of 25 August, so the passage was also back in between, outside the pack. Candidates c09 (first version; the critique section in the same run is i11, and E76's -219 edit only shortened text) and c31. Not level 3: one editor, one article, one re-insertion visible in the pack.

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds a section criticising the 'noble' motive of Greater Finland: Finland's Sami languages and culture were Finnicised much as the Finnic peoples beyond the eastern border were Russified.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted: 'Saamelaisten kieli, elinkeinot ja kulttuuri ovat suomalaistuneet aika samalla tavalla kuin itärajan takaiset suomensukuisia kieliä puhuvat ovat venäläistyneet. Tämä seikka saattaa ylläolevan jalon motiivin hieman arveluttavaan valoon.' ('The Sami language, livelihoods and culture have been Finnicised in much the same way as the Finnic-speaking peoples beyond the eastern border have been Russified. This puts the noble motive above in a somewhat dubious light.'): an argument written as a reply to i10 (summary 'vastine motiivikysymykseen', 'a reply on the motive question'). Community dispute: the removal summary is about neutrality, 'puppua poistettu, tämä ei ole pamflettisivusto' ('nonsense removed, this is not a pamphlet site'). Added by E75 (194.157.x.x) on 2005-08-04, removed together with i10 by E8 about 16 h later. E76's edit in between (351774, 130.232.x.x, 'etninen puhdistus hieman kohtuuton termi', 'ethnic cleansing a somewhat excessive term') only shortened the section and is not an insertion. Candidate c09. Not level 3: one editor, one article, never put back. Weakest level-2 item in this topic: the only dispute signal is that shared removal summary.

items.label: contested
items.description: Restores a reworded version of the Greater Finland article that adds a paragraph on what was fatal to the Karelian language, replaces the sentence on Finnish Reds assimilating Karelians and Vepsians into Finns with 'disagreements over the official language', and softens how East Karelians saw the Finns as occupiers.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted: '1930-luvulla oli erimielisyyksiä Neuvosto-Karjalan virallisesta kielestä' ('in the 1930s there were disagreements over Soviet Karelia's official language') in place of 'karjalaiset ja vepsäläiset haluttiin suomalaisten punaisten käsissä olleen työväenkommuunin kautta sulauttaa suomalaisiin' ('Karelians and Vepsians were to be assimilated into Finns through the workers' commune held by Finnish Reds'), and 'suhtautuivat jopa paikoin suomalaisiin kuin miehittäjiin' ('in places even regarded the Finns as occupiers') in place of '... pikemminkin kuin miehittäjiin' ('... rather as occupiers'): it changes who is said to have assimilated whom and how East Karelians saw the Finnish occupation. Community dispute: the edit took the {{kiistanalainen}} (disputed) template off the article during an edit war (22 identity reverts on the page within 3 days), and the removal restored the template: 'palautus, kiistanalaisuustagin laiton jälkeen tehty perusteeton palautus ja laaja muutos' ('revert: an unfounded restoration and broad change made after the dispute tag was added'); the removal was itself undone once (393866), and the text is not in the latest revision. Added by E74 (130.233.x.x, summary 'palautettu neutraloituun näkökulmaan', 'restored to a neutralised point of view') on 2005-08-27, removed by E8 11.8 h later. E83's three small edits and E12's two see-also edits in the same run are dropped. Candidate c14. Not level 3: one editor, one article.

items.label: contested
items.description: Adds that Finland gave little help to East Karelia partly because of Finland's internal fragmentation after the White Terror, later citing the front page of the Finnish president's website, and drops 'radical' from the lead's definition of the Greater Finland idea.
items.why: Level 2. Claim, quoted: 'Syy siihen, miksi Suomesta ei saatu laajaa apua johtuu osittain Suomen sisäisestä fragmentoitumisesta Valkoisen Terrorin jälkeen' ('The reason why no broad help came from Finland is partly Finland's internal fragmentation after the White Terror'), re-added with a reference to presidentti.fi titled 'Etusivu' ('front page'); the same run deletes 'radikaali' from 'heimoaatteen radikaali muoto' ('the radical form of the kinship ideology') and changes 'mahdollisesti' ('possibly') to 'harvemmin' ('less often') for Norwegian and Swedish areas. Community dispute: both removals are about sourcing, 'Lähteetöntä' ('unsourced', E42) and 'ei vastaa lähdettä' ('does not match the source', E126); put back once, 55 days after the first removal (summary 'Tämä on faktaa. Ken ei historiaa tunne voi ottaa selvää', 'This is fact. Whoever does not know history can look it up'). One named account (E129) on 2026-01-30 and 2026-03-26; versions stayed 24 min and 7.1 h. Candidates c27, c10. Not level 3: one account, one article, put back only once; the unrelated citation is the sources signal, but level 3 also needs an editors or articles signal.

items.label: reverted
items.description: Moves Käkisalmi to Finland in the infobox and lead (country 'Suomi', region 'Suomen alue', the city 'had to be ceded to Finland'), changes the founding year from 1944 to 1941 and the municipality template to 'Russian'.
items.why: Level 1. Substantive changes of country, region, wording and a date by an anonymous editor (E288, 84.250.x.x) on 2023-04-15, taken out by a different account (E42) on 2023-05-23, 38 days later, with no summary. Coherent and consistent in one direction ('Laatokan rantakaupunki entisellä Suomen alueella', 'jouduttiin luovuttamaan Suomelle', 'a Ladoga shore town on former Finnish territory', 'had to be ceded to Finland'), so judged as content, not graffiti; it contradicts the rest of the article, which places the city in Russia. No dispute signal: no removal reason, never put back, no template. The other edits in the run (21524938 by E289, 21525210 and 21525215 by E259) add an unrelated image and are item n01. Candidate c03.

items.label: reverted
items.description: Reformats the city's names in other languages in the lead (Karelian and Russian name templates) and adds its Russian names by period: Кексгольм 1611-1918 and 1940-1948, Кякисалми 1918-1940.
items.why: Level 1, capped. Substantive (names and dates), taken out twice by a different account (E137) and put back once by E21 (3161128, a rollback to E286's version). Not a claim: the added name forms and periods carry no slant and no removal says they are wrong; the removal summaries are about conduct, 'Toivon, että käyttäjä ... ei ole aloittamassa palautussotaa' ('I hope the user is not starting a revert war'), and a link to the 'be bold' guideline. A formatting dispute does not reach level 2. Added by E286 on 2007-07-13 (summary 'nimet muilla kielillä', 'names in other languages'). Candidates c13, c07.

items.label: reverted
items.description: Adds a section 'Käkisalmi is nowadays Priozersk' quoting a Russian source on the 1948 renaming, and changes the Russian-name history in the lead to '1611-1948 Кексгольм'.
items.why: Level 1, capped. Substantive (sourced text and dates), taken out after 6 min by a different account (E12) with '...jota itse sinne tunget' ('...which you yourself keep putting there'); the edit was itself a re-insertion and the removal was undone again (1621449), so the section went back and forth. Not counted as a claim: the 1948 renaming is already in the lead and is sourced here; the dispute is about emphasis, and no removal says the text is wrong or not neutral. The lead change drops the 1918-1940 period from the Russian-name history, a minor change. Added by E285 (summary 'Nimenmuutoksen toteaminen samoin kuin Primorskin (ent. Koivisto) artikkelissa', 'stating the renaming as in the Primorsk (formerly Koivisto) article'). Candidate c32.

items.label: not-incident
items.description: Adds a mid-19th-century image of Käkisalmi from Topelius's 'Finland framställdt i teckningar' to the article, with two small follow-up edits.
items.why: Excluded: kept. The image line went out only because E42 reverted the article to its state before E288's edit (i14); the same line is in the latest revision (flag added_text_in_latest_revision), so the community kept it. Note: the removal was not undone by an identity revert (flag removal_was_itself_undone is not set); a later edit restored the line. E259's two small edits (+23 and -4 bytes, 2 h after E289's) are not visible separately in the pack; by timing and size they are taken as tweaks to the same image entry. Candidate c03 (contains must-include 21525215).

items.label: not-incident
items.description: Replaces every 'Karjala' in the article with a nonsense word; summary 'Vitsi. Palautetaan ihan kohta.' ('A joke. Will be restored right away.').
items.why: Excluded: self-removal. The same anonymous editor (E180) undid it 59 s later. It would also be graffiti, but self-removal comes first in the exclusion order. Candidate c34.

items.why: Excluded: blanking (-9,409 bytes; the page content was replaced with 'lol'), undone by a different account after 48 s. Candidate c37.

items.label: not-incident

items.why: Excluded: not substantive. The edit adds one internal link to the see-also list and no prose, number, date, name or citation; removed after 5 min with 'ei pidä kehottaa katsomaan, kun ei ole mitä katsoa' ('readers should not be told to see something when there is nothing to see'). Candidate c38.

items.label: not-incident
items.description: Re-aligns the whitespace of the Viipuri infobox parameters.

items.label: not-incident
items.description: Adds a copyright-check maintenance template ({{Tekijänoikeus_201009|diff=900}}).
items.why: Excluded: not substantive (a template only). Added by a bot-like account (E104) and removed after the check ('ok') 20 days later; not-substantive comes before bot in the exclusion order. Candidate c36.

items.label: not-incident
items.description: The undone edit deletes an external-links subsection with two blogs supporting the Greater Finland idea; the 'removal' puts the links back.
items.why: Excluded: not substantive. The undone edit (394261, -174 bytes) adds nothing; it only deletes two external links, and the 'removal' (394272, E83) restores them, arguing that the links belong to the subject. Nothing was added and later taken out in this run. The links were deleted again afterwards (394281). Candidate c40.

items.label: not-incident
items.description: The undone edit is a rollback that deletes the sentence 'in the Second World War Germany promised to give Finland the Belgian Congo'; the anonymous editor put the sentence back 4 s later.
items.why: Excluded: not substantive. The undone edit (414455, a rollback by E5, -67 bytes) adds no text; it only deletes the joke sentence 'Toisessa mailmansodassa saksa lupasi antaa suomelle Belgian Kongon' ('in the Second World War Germany promised to give Finland the Belgian Congo'), which E85 (62.183.x.x) put back 4 s later (414456) and a later edit removed again (414465). The joke sentence itself would be graffiti; its insertions are not inserting edits in the pack. Candidate c41.

topic.notes: Labelled from the pack only.
